Compatibility and limitations

GL Lab compiles C11 and C++17 with Emscripten 3.1.24 in your browser. Generated JavaScript and WebAssembly run on your device. Legacy OpenGL uses GL4ES 1.1.7 to draw through WebGL.

AreaAvailableCurrent limit
C and C++Real compiler diagnostics, standard libraries, console output and a virtual filesystem.The editor opens one source file at a time. Arbitrary desktop packages, native executables and operating-system APIs are unavailable.
OpenGLGL4ES translates supported legacy drawing, matrices and rendering state to WebGL. GLUT and GLFW sources select the needed compatibility libraries automatically.This is not a complete desktop OpenGL driver. Supported rendering depends on GL4ES, WebGL and the browser. A reported OpenGL version does not guarantee every API or extension.
GLUT, GLU and GLFWA single graphics canvas with browser callbacks. Compatibility helpers preserve the existing GLUT source workflow.Desktop window placement, multiple native windows and full freeglut/GLU coverage are unavailable. See the verification scope below.
Input and filesSupply text in the console's Input panel before Run for scanf or cin. Programs can create and read in-memory files.Input is supplied once per run, not through an interactive terminal. Program files disappear when the run is disposed. Host filesystem access is not provided.
Graphics controlsCanvas keyboard/mouse input, PNG export, fullscreen and a separate output view.The editor receives canvas frames at up to about 30 fps; the separate output view mirrors at up to about 15 fps. The program's own loop can run at a different rate.
Build optionsExtra compiler arguments and downloadable generated JavaScript/Wasm.The workspace controls output names and runtime settings. It does not provide a project build system or a package installer. Exported files need a web page to load the generated module.
Phones and resourcesCompilation and rendering take place on the visiting device. The public site needs no Tailscale connection or desktop server.First use loads about 25 MB of compiler tools plus the selected libraries. Compilation can consume hundreds of MB of memory. Device/browser limits can prevent larger programs from compiling.

Event loops must yield

Use GLUT callbacks or emscripten_set_main_loop for animation. A desktop while loop that never yields can freeze the browser tab. Stop can terminate compilation and cooperative running programs, but cannot reliably interrupt JavaScript or WebAssembly that blocks the tab's event loop.

SDK and threading

This deployment pins Emscripten 3.1.24 and GL4ES 1.1.7. It is not the latest Emscripten SDK. The browser compiler is single-threaded; pthread/SharedArrayBuffer builds are outside the supported workspace configuration. Newer Emscripten ports and settings may be unavailable.

Verification scope

The merge checks compile and execute source through the same Compiler and Runner used by the editor. They cover C console input, C++ standard-library and virtual-file operations, legacy GLUT/GLU drawing, GLFW, canvas pixels, keyboard input, compile-error recovery and stop/restart. This scope does not establish support for every OpenGL function, shader, extension or physical phone.

Keep your source

Existing drafts remain under the same browser and domain. Drafts are local to that browser. Download or copy important code before clearing browser data or switching devices. The compiler does not upload your source to a compilation server.

Components

Emscripten via Emception, LLVM/Clang, Binaryen, GL4ES and CodeMirror. Licenses and source provenance are included with the hosted assets.
